item.title: And, bhikkhus, what is dwelling in heedfulness? One who lives restraining the eye faculty, bhikkhus, his mind is not stained by forms cognizable by the…
item.description:
And, bhikkhus, what is dwelling in heedfulness? One who lives restraining the eye faculty, bhikkhus, his mind is not stained by forms cognizable by the eye. For one with an unstained mind, gladness arises. With gladness, rapture arises. With rapture, the body becomes tranquil. With a tranquil body, he experiences happiness. For one who is happy, the mind becomes concentrated. With concentration, phenomena become manifest. When phenomena are manifest, that person is called one who dwells in heedfulness. ... the ear faculty ... the nose faculty ... the tongue faculty ... the body faculty ... One who lives restraining the mind faculty, his mind is not stained by mind-objects cognizable by the mind. For one with an unstained mind, gladness arises. With gladness, rapture arises. With rapture, the body becomes tranquil. With a tranquil body, he experiences happiness. For one who is happy, the mind becomes concentrated. With concentration, phenomena become manifest. When phenomena are manifest, that person is called one who dwells in heedfulness. Thus, bhikkhus, is dwelling in heedfulness.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.97

item.title: Poṭṭhapāda, when defiled states are abandoned and pure states increase, one in this very life, with direct knowledge, attains and abides in full and extensive…
item.description:
Poṭṭhapāda, when defiled states are abandoned and pure states increase, one in this very life, with direct knowledge, attains and abides in full and extensive wisdom, then joy arises, gladness, tranquility, mindfulness, clear comprehension, and a pleasant abiding arise.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 9 – Poṭṭhapādasutta

item.title: Just as, bhikkhus, in the autumn, when the sky is clear and cloudless, the sun rises in the sky, dispelling all darkness from space, shining,…
item.description:
Just as, bhikkhus, in the autumn, when the sky is clear and cloudless, the sun rises in the sky, dispelling all darkness from space, shining, glowing, and radiating. So too, bhikkhus, by developing and cultivating the perception of impermanence, all sensual lust is abandoned, all lust for form is abandoned, all craving for existence is abandoned, all ignorance is abandoned, all conceit is uprooted. How is the perception of impermanence developed and cultivated, bhikkhus, so that all sensual lust is abandoned ... all conceit is uprooted? This is form; this is the arising of form; this is the cessation of form. This is feeling ... this is perception ... these are formations ... this is consciousness; this is the arising of consciousness; this is the cessation of consciousness. The perception of impermanence developed and cultivated in this way, bhikkhus, leads to the abandoning of all sensual lust, all lust for form, all craving for existence, all ignorance, and the uprooting of all conceit.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.102

item.title: Because of robes, bhikkhus, craving arises for a bhikkhu. Because of almsfood, bhikkhus, craving arises for a bhikkhu. Because of lodgings, bhikkhus, craving arises for…
item.description:
Because of robes, bhikkhus, craving arises for a bhikkhu. Because of almsfood, bhikkhus, craving arises for a bhikkhu. Because of lodgings, bhikkhus, craving arises for a bhikkhu. Because of this or that kind of existence, bhikkhus, craving arises for a bhikkhu. These are the four kinds of arising of craving from which craving arises for a bhikkhu.

One with craving as companion
Wanders for a long time.
He does not transcend the round of existence,
From this life to the next.

Knowing this danger,
That craving gives birth to suffering,
Free from craving, without clinging,
Mindful, the bhikkhu wanders.

From: Itivuttaka 105

item.title: Bhikkhus, in the future, bhikkhus will desire delicious almsfood. Because they desire delicious almsfood, they will abandon the almsfood round, abandon the forests, the remote…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, in the future, bhikkhus will desire delicious almsfood. Because they desire delicious almsfood, they will abandon the almsfood round, abandon the forests, the remote highland dwellings, and go to villages, towns, and royal cities, dwelling there, seeking exquisite flavors with their tongues. Because of almsfood, they will fall into improper, unsuitable seeking. This, bhikkhus, is the second fear regarding the future, not yet arisen now but will arise in the future. You should fully understand them. Having fully understood them, you should strive to abandon that fear.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.80

item.title: - Friend Sāriputta, what things should a virtuous bhikkhu attend to wisely? - Friend Kotthika, a virtuous bhikkhu should attend wisely to the five aggregates…
item.description:
- Friend Sāriputta, what things should a virtuous bhikkhu attend to wisely? - Friend Kotthika, a virtuous bhikkhu should attend wisely to the five aggregates of clinging as impermanent, suffering, a disease, a boil, a dart, a calamity, an affliction, alien, breaking up, empty, and non-self. What are the five? That is, the form aggregate of clinging, the feeling aggregate of clinging, the perception aggregate of clinging, the formation aggregate of clinging, the consciousness aggregate of clinging. Friend Kotthika, a virtuous bhikkhu should attend wisely to the five aggregates of clinging as impermanent, suffering, a disease, a boil, a dart, a calamity, an affliction, alien, breaking up, empty, and non-self.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.122

item.title: One who among all beings Understands liberation From the trap of death, For the happiness of devas and humans, Declares the noble truth, Declares the…
item.description:
One who among all beings
Understands liberation
From the trap of death,
For the happiness of devas and humans,
Declares the noble truth,
Declares the true Dhamma.
The multitude seeing and hearing this
Rejoice with serene faith.
Skilled in the path and non-path,
What should be done has been done,
Taintless, Enlightened,
With this last body,
He is called by name,
Great Wisdom, Great Man.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.35

item.title: Just as, bhikkhus, a person were to take the grass, sticks, branches, and leaves of this Jeta's Grove, and burn them or use them as…
item.description:
Just as, bhikkhus, a person were to take the grass, sticks, branches, and leaves of this Jeta's Grove, and burn them or use them as he wishes. Would you think: 'That person takes us, burns us, or uses us as he wishes'?" — "No, Venerable Sir. Why is that? Because that is not us. Venerable Sir, that is not our self." — "So too, bhikkhus, form is not yours, abandon it. Abandoning it will lead to your long-term welfare and happiness. Feeling is not yours ... Perception is not yours ... Formations are not yours ... Consciousness is not yours, abandon it. Abandoning it will lead to your long-term welfare and happiness.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.33

item.title: Just as, bhikkhus, in a king's frontier fortress there is a moat, both deep and wide, to protect those inside the fortress and to keep…
item.description:
Just as, bhikkhus, in a king's frontier fortress there is a moat, both deep and wide, to protect those inside the fortress and to keep out those outside. So too, bhikkhus, a noble disciple has moral shame. He is ashamed of evil bodily action, evil verbal action, evil mental action. He is ashamed of falling into evil, unwholesome states. Using moral shame as the moat, bhikkhus, the noble disciple abandons the unwholesome, develops the wholesome, abandons what is blameworthy, develops what is blameless, and keeps himself pure. With this second excellent quality he is accomplished.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 7.67

item.title: Elder Vacchapāla: If one sees the truth, wonderful, subtle, With wisdom skillfully, with humble mind, Living according to the virtue prescribed by the Buddha, Nibbāna…
item.description:
Elder Vacchapāla:

If one sees the truth, wonderful, subtle,
With wisdom skillfully, with humble mind,
Living according to the virtue prescribed by the Buddha,
Nibbāna is not hard to attain for that one.

From: Theragāthā 1.71
